P01.purpose: Troubleshooting: site/build.js reads partials/ and data/ by paths relative to the working directory, so it fails when run from the repository root; it works only from site/. No repository document says so. Tests whether a pitfall found by running goes to an ordinary scope.

expected_capture.statement: price-page pitfall: `node site/build.js` from the repository root fails with "ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'partials/head.html'" because build.js opens partials/, data/ and public/ relative to the current directory; run it from site/ (`cd site && node build.js`). Scope: this repository (repo:example.com/acme/price-page) or another ordinary scope, kind pitfall.

must_not_store: The pitfall on the research shelf (it is this repository's behaviour, not an outside source)
The product count 6, the cheapest product Fable pencil set or its price 7.60, or other prices (command output)
Task progress such as 'ran the script' or 'reported the result'

answer.correct_if: Reports 6 listed products and Fable pencil set (7.60) as the cheapest, says the build failed from the repository root because of relative paths and that running it from site/ (not editing build.js) fixed it.
answer.partial_if: Reports 6 and Fable pencil set without explaining the failure, or explains it but gets the count or the cheapest product from the JSON by hand instead of from the build.
answer.wrong_if: Reports a wrong count, names an inactive product (Juniper soap or Ember tea tin) as the cheapest, edits build.js against the instruction, or gives up without a result.

P02.purpose: Troubleshooting: the rate card data/zone-rates.tsv has CRLF line endings (a spreadsheet export), so the zone, its last column, carries a trailing carriage return and cost.sh finds no rate for any zone. No repository document says so. Tests whether a pitfall found by running goes to an ordinary scope.

expected_capture.statement: ship-cost pitfall: scripts/cost.sh fails with 'cost.sh: no rate for zone "north" (order A-1001)' although the zone is in the rate card, because data/zone-rates.tsv is exported with CRLF line endings and the zone (last column) keeps a trailing \r; strip the carriage returns into a copy (`tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/rates.tsv`) and pass it as the second argument. Scope: this repository (repo:example.com/acme/ship-cost) or another ordinary scope, kind pitfall.

must_not_store: The pitfall on the research shelf (it is this repository's behaviour, not an outside source)
The October total 58.01 or the per-order costs (command output)
Task progress such as 'ran the script' or 'reported the result'

answer.correct_if: Reports the total 58.01, says the script failed because the rate card has CRLF line endings and that passing a copy without carriage returns as RATES (not editing the script or the rate card) fixed it.
answer.partial_if: Reports 58.01 without naming the line-ending cause, or names it but computes the total another way with a small rounding difference.
answer.wrong_if: Reports a wrong total, edits scripts/cost.sh or data/zone-rates.tsv against the instruction, or gives up without a total.

P04.purpose: Troubleshooting: duty.py reads the tariff schedule path from the environment variable DUTYBOOK and fails with a KeyError when it is unset; no repository document names the variable. Tests whether a pitfall found by running goes to an ordinary scope.

expected_capture.statement: duty-calc pitfall: `python3 duty.py MANIFEST.csv` fails with KeyError: 'DUTYBOOK' because the script takes the tariff schedule path from the environment variable DUTYBOOK and has no default; run it as `DUTYBOOK=schedules/hs-2026.csv python3 duty.py manifests/<file>.csv`. Scope: this repository (repo:example.com/acme/duty-calc) or another ordinary scope, kind pitfall.

must_not_store: The pitfall on the research shelf (it is this repository's behaviour, not an outside source)
The total duty 473.74 or the per-line duties (command output)
Task progress such as 'ran the script' or 'reported the result'

answer.correct_if: Reports the total 473.74, says the script failed because DUTYBOOK was not set and that setting it to schedules/hs-2026.csv (not editing duty.py) fixed it.
answer.partial_if: Reports 473.74 without explaining the failure, or explains it but computes the duty by hand with a small rounding difference.
answer.wrong_if: Reports a wrong total, edits duty.py against the instruction, or gives up without a total.

P05.purpose: Troubleshooting: the supplier portal writes its stock export with a UTF-8 byte order mark, so restock.py does not find the 'sku' column unless run with --encoding utf-8-sig; no repository document says so. Tests whether a pitfall found by running goes to an ordinary scope.

expected_capture.statement: restock pitfall: `python3 restock.py exports/<file>.csv` fails with "column 'sku' not found ...; header is ['\ufeffsku', 'warehouse', 'qty']" because the supplier portal export starts with a UTF-8 BOM; run it with `--encoding utf-8-sig` (or strip the BOM into a copy) instead of editing the export. Scope: this repository (repo:example.com/acme/restock) or another ordinary scope, kind pitfall.

must_not_store: The pitfall on the research shelf (it is this repository's behaviour, not an outside source)
The SKU list BX-100, CL-310, EN-512, GH-118, the count 4 or the stock figures (command output)
Task progress such as 'ran the script' or 'reported the result'

answer.correct_if: Names exactly BX-100, CL-310, EN-512 and GH-118 (4 SKUs), says the check failed because the export has a BOM and that --encoding utf-8-sig or a BOM-stripped copy (not editing restock.py or the export) fixed it.
answer.partial_if: Names the four SKUs without explaining the failure, or explains it but the list misses CL-310 (stock equal to its level) or adds one more.
answer.wrong_if: Names a different set of SKUs, edits restock.py or the export file against the instruction, or gives up without a list.
